I'm quite surprised how amazing this game is.
The single player was one hell of a ride. Extremely enjoyable ride. Ride full of slashing limbs and making big holes in torsos and vaporizing hundreds and thousands (definitely thousands) of green skins and heretics.
The combat mechanics are nothing new, but they are well polished and the killing enemies is satisfactory. The melee fighting in large groups of foes could take some work because your character starts to stutter when he is being hit from every possible side and angle. But it's still better than being surrounded by group of enemies and being attacked only by one at a time (ehm ehm AC ehm ehm). Shooting experience is also really good, as is the feeling of watching explosion of blood after a bolt from your weapon penetrates the body of your target. The execution mode which regenerates health by finishing enemies has nice range of incredibly good looking animations.
The weapon progression is slow but steady. You have 4 different melee weapons and 10 ranged weapons at your disposal. Through out the game you'll find fury seals (something like a berserker mode) which will upgrade your ability. But only with something incremental as longer fury time, or regenerating HP by inflicting damage. Those are nice things to have, but there could be something more interesting gameplay wise. The steady progression comes to a halt few chapters before the end of the game, which is kinda sad. There are also few instances where you have a jetpack, whit which you can propel yourself up into the air, find a group of foes and fall down on them dealing massive damage, stunning them and looking at the awesome shockwave.
The level design isn't anything special or even good. It's a corridor with a lot of curves and vertical traverses. But even though  it isn't great from gameplay point of view, the game has an amazing atmosphere. I love postapo and I could feel it everywhere I've went. It was awesome, the heavy feeling that this world is doomed and that there is no hope for civilians. And that I'm here to help however I can, fighting "alone" against the never ending hordes. This is nicely complemented by a atmospheric soundtrack.
The story isn't something special, it's your generic shooter story with a villain and wanna be twist waiting for you somewhere. But I would say that for a WH40k fan it has to be really enjoyable. It's a game that is suppose to be pure fun and relax, not something to think about, so I don't see a problem with the story line. The only weak point was the final boss fight which was a dull sequence of the same QTEs over and over again.
There isn't anyone in the multi player right now which is sad. Because when I've played it with friends few years ago it was great fun. There are some basic modes like versus (team against team) or you can play some parts of the story (I don't think it's the whole story, but I can't remember) with a group of friends.
My conclusion is that it's a great entertaining game, pure fun from killing thousands of enemies and I can recommend it to everyone.
8.7/10 (I like the number 7)

WH40K Space Marine is a 3rd person combat game that has you, as Ultramarine Captain Titus, wade your way using guns, grenades, and melee weapons through enemies of the Imperium, such as (but not limited to) the Orks. The game starts with space sensors detecting Ork ships approaching Forge World Graia and the only ones in range to respond in time was Captain Titus, along with Sergeant Sidonus, and rookie Tech Marine Leandros. They wade their way into battle, fighting their way through Ork lines to reach the Imperial Guard on the surface, and accomplished several missions such as disabling the space cannon captured by the Orks, as well as reach Inquisitor Drogan who claimed to have a weapon that can wipe the Orks off the planet, only to discover an even greater threat hiding in the wings...
Captain Titus is a veteran fighter and knows all the moves, including bashing, slicing, and more, as well as seamlessly switching between gunplay and melee. On the other hand, there are tons of Orks around, various types, from shooters to melee to minibosses to true level bosses.
Enemies can be shot or blasted with grenades, but the most visceral way of dispatching enemies is with melee, as you will yield vibroblade, power axe, and even shockhammer into combat. Enemies can also be stunned THEN "fatalized" with a fatality / execution, which is the only way for you to regain health.
There are occasional segments that involve a rocket pack, for you to jump up and bypass many walls, ledges, and such. Yet others have you use fixed heavy guns against enemies, and Ork gunships, and even rip off the heavy guns and use them as limited-ammo miniguns the enemies in your way. Grenades can be used to flush enemies out of cover. And there are various types of guns, from short-range stormers to ultra-long sniper rifles.
The levels are detailed, and characters are very nicely digitized. There are hidden collectibles you can find all around the levels that will unlock bonus powers, and new eapons and abilities are unlocked at a steady pace.
The moves are exquisite, with the different melee weapons were all wielded with very different combat styles. Vibroblades are stabbed and swung, but axes and hammers are swung hard and knock enemies back, and each weapon has different set of pros and cons, such as power vs. swing speed vs. weapon change speed.
You don't always fight alone. Sometimes your fellow ultramarines are on your side, while others have you fighting alongside the Imperial Guards. yet other time you will find yourself watching the other two factions fight and you decide who should be your target.
The game sometimes gets extremely frustrating when it gives you a gunship that is highly resistant against the fire you're putting out, WHILE the gunship drops enemies behind you, yet on other levels the game is perfectly balanced, not too easy so it's no longer a challenge, but never hard enough to make you want to rage quit.
All in all, if you like WH40K and/or 3rd person combat games that involves no jumping, you should give this a try.

I really like this game, but then, I am a 40K fanboy.
The game is a linear, point to point slaughter fest. A lot of the negative reviews mention it is repetitive it is. Then again so is every shooter in recent years.
What the game does have is faithful to the lore art and information, great sound effects and a combat system that seamlessly switches between ranged combat and melee. The combat is visceral and very satisfying.  Despite being nearly four years old the engine has aged well.
It is, I find amusing, that some reviews talk about the story being basic when the vast majority of games available are even worse and titles with grander production values fair worse. This game isn't Deus Ex and nor is it Wolfenstein Old Blood, i,e the only two shooters I can remember that have a good campaign.  It is satisfying, fit for purpose and gives you an excuse to kill lots of things.
There are a number of enemy unit types in the game and most of the core Ork units are there, boyz, nobz, weirdboyz, gretchin, ard boyz and the warboss. Chaos units are fairly limited to psyers, cultist, tactical and devestator marines, champions and Khorne bloodletters.
The campaign is the usual 7-8 hours odd depending on how much time you spend looking for things and difficulty you play on. This is pretty much standard to most Single Player games.
The game is very well presented and polished. Negative reviews mention a number of issues, AI, geometry and scripting errors and I've yet to come across any issues, nada not one.
One down side is the multiplayer which can be difficult to find games on, although it does have a large amount of customisation it could do with more variety. Even the horde mode is quite limited and perhaps should have went down the Dawn of War 2 route and allowed players to also play as Orks and Imperial Guard.
I've gifted copies to friends and family to try and drag them into the game.
Space Marine is game I will play again and again, it is the perfect game to just to unwind with, slaughter a few Orks and move on.
I recommend this game

I'm writing a negative review not for the actual game itself, but for the poor version I inadvertedly purchased as a German buyer. You see, in Germany, we still have very narrow views on what is acceptable or harmful in a video game. This game gives new meaning to the phrase "One More Turn"!  I've been a fan of the total war series for a long time.  From Rome Total War to this game, I've always enjoyed each total war game to an extent.  Total War Warhammer 2 is one of the best total war games in the series.
Story: The main single player campaign focuses on four factions (high elves, dark elves, skaven and the lizard men) in their quest for the power of the vortex.  Simple straightforward story.  There are no big cutscenes or deep character stories but it gives you an objective.
Gameplay: The main campaign map is huge.  What makes it different fromt he first  is that there are several landmasses and islands.  You will definitely have to transport your armies via sea in many scenarios.  It kind of is sad given that there are several islands that sea battles were not included.  The real time battles on land though are awesome.  Having my high elven warriors clash with dark elves and skaven looked awesome!  If you are new to total war games, thee are definitely some things are tricks you have to learn like which units are effective against certain enemies and moving your forces correctly into position, even when outnumbered (at least take thousands of them with you).
Note: If you have the original total war, you can expand the total war 2 map with the mortal empire campaign which combines the first total war warhammer map with the total war warhammer 2 map.  This is an awesome feature giving you so many hours of play!  Now I can conquer the world as the mortal humans or high elves!
Overall: This is one of the best strategy games on the PC this year.  If you are looking for a good strategy game to play.  Definitely check this out.

When I was a kid, I never dreamt about nightmares from bad movies like my other kid frineds. Instead in the middle of the night, my dad would wake me up and play maortal kombat 1 with me. It got to the point where it was the only thing I thought about before I went to bed.
Now I'm substantially older and despite thinking about other things a little more, fighting games wtill hold a special place in my heart. Well...GOOD fighting games rather. Mortal Kombat 9 has popped up with the old flair it once had, but I still feel like something's missing, Blazblue is SUPER fun, but not available for PC, so of course I was just in the dust because I've never particularly liked Street Fighter.
BACKGROUND:
So then Skullgirls pops onto PC, a port I've literally waited/anticipated years for. The port is WONDERFUL. The effort everyone puts into it is phenominal. Honestly. Coming from a crowdfunding IndieGoGo campaign raising almost a million dollars and NOT being Street Fighter, it's kind of a big deal.
Hand-drawn visuals are the only thing to grace this game and it never gets old seeing each frame of animation play out...unless you're losing probably lol. While playing BlazBlue I used to occasionally play in Mike Z's lobby when he got on, but I didn't really know who he was at the time. Apparently he was like a fighting god who was a real force in gaming & I held my own against his Tager, winning and losing equally. But little did I know HE would be the guy to give input on Skullgirls and help make it, basically making it his new way to live.
SYSTEM:
Skullgirls takes out a lot of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t and just includes what's "necessary" for hardcore 2D fighters. Although there are 1 or 2 features/mechanics I wish were in the game (and might be on their way in the future), I've been pretty happy with what we have so far. everything is very straightforward and no 1-frame link ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t unless you want to make a custom combo yourself with unusual timing. And THAT'S another t hing. YOU can make combos the way you want. Implemented is something called IPS (Infinite Prevention System) that keeps people from performing infinites. Now this doesnt mean you won't get your♥♥♥♥♥whipped or long combos are out the game....quite the opposite, but it DOES mean everything is FAIR. If someone resets a combo, you'll know because of visual cues. If you keep getting hit before your attack comes out, the game will let you know with a red flash over your character, telling you you were just a biiiiit too slow and got counterhit. The system is simple, yet has depth for hardcore gamers as well.
GAMEPLAY:
To bring something new to fighting games, skullgirls combines the 6-button gameplay of something like street fighter, but mixes it with the combo-heavy nature of games like a BlazBlue. And also a really cool team-system is used. If you like playing solo with one character, you can use a REALLY strong character who has incredible damage, or trade a little bit of that for a team of 2, with regeneration when tagged out, invaluable tag assists, and Delayed Hyper combos. Things like make fighting games. It plays like BUTTER and the sense of impact is PERFECT. When you hit someone with a strong attack, you will definitely feel it. And I really like that. Wonderful sound design, everything.
CONCLUSION:
And speaking of hardcore gamers, the general pool of people who play this is one of quality. You will definitely be facing some good competition. And I'm very happy about that. So if you want to play this game, I definitely recommened it. The people are GREAT and will help you if you need it, and with nothing but more good features coming to it, it'd be best to hop on now while it's still early!

I played the demo for this game back when it first came out on the Wii and instantaneously fell in love with it. The super-hip use of the retro-esque style really caught my eye. Not to mention I'm a sucker for colorful things. Although the look of BIT.TRIP RUNNER is what brought my attention to this game... it was the awesome, tight controls that made me stay. It's a great mix of platforming, style, and controls that anyone who can appreciate those things should consider picking it up.
The aesthetics and minimal-yet amazing controls aren't the only great things about BIT.TRIP RUNNER! The music for this game is also magnificent. Little beats come out whenever you successfully pass an obstacle. It's so cool. It really makes you feel like you're a part of the game, as though you are orchestrating these really cool tunes. Personally, it's the game's best feature.
Despite it being such a cool game, at times it CAN be a bit frusterating. Especially if you aren't particularly great at platformers (I have no problems there, considering I'm a wiz at platformers!) You'll find yourself getting screwed over by obstacles that you don't know are coming, which will take you back to the beginning of the level. But then you'll know what's in store for you! So don't give up!
And getting to the finish line is one of the most satisfying things.
All in all, I have deep appreciation for the game, and this review was more a way for me to publicly gush about this game than it is a review. If you're reading this, you already know that I think this game is great. So go try it for yourself and see if you like it! BIT.TRIP RUNNER is one of those games that everyone should at least try once. It'll show you that there are some amazing indie games out there!

I'll give my review for zombies and multiplayer as I haven't completed the campaign yet.
This is where the game really shines for me. I have over 25 days played on Black Ops 3 zombies thanks to the season pass maps and chronicles. So I'm quite a big zombies fan. I'm not gonna review the DLC maps, because it would take far too long for me to do so. All you need to know about them is that, IN MY OPINION, some of the maps are better than Treyarch maps. Especially Spaceland, Rave and Attack.
Infinity Ward had some really good improvements over Treyarch zombies. Every single trap is unique in it's own way, all DLC-weapons were added to weapon loadouts and to every zombies map, none of the Fate and Fortune cards were OP as hell, the ranking system doesn't have prestiges but it has 999 levels, and the weapon variants from multiplayer keep the zombies-experience fresh and interesting.
I also like how they changed a few game-mechanics inside of zombies. You don't really get stuck on zombies anymore, as you can just kinda squeeze through them, but the zombies hit faster and are overall just more aggressive. I also prefer the new double PaP mechanic over Treyarch's Alternate Ammo Types. In IW, the double PaP just makes the weapon a bit powerful and gives it more ammo, so it isn't stupidly broken like AAT was in Black Ops 3.
Then the characters. I have an unpopular opinion on this matter, as I actually like these characters and the way they were handled. The characters have a different personality in each map, which I really enjoy. For example, Poindexter is a nerd in Spaceland, but in Shaolin, Poindexter pretty much screams "♥♥♥♥ you!" What I don't like about them, is the lack of real character development behind them. But I really don't mind that, as the characters are entertaining to play as.
The soundtrack in zombies is, in my opinion, the biggest improvement from Treyarch zombies. Every map has a unique setlist fitting the theme of the map, and most of the songs are fantastic. It also gives you something to listen to while playing.
Zombies in Spaceland is a fantastic on-disk map. It has so much replay-value it's unbelievable. You have all kinds of side quests that you can do, but they aren't mandatory to get to a high round or just do well in general. I went to round 30 on my very first playthrough without even knowing about the Weapons of Rock (granted I'm a pretty good zombies-player)
I think the boss zombie (Brute) is one of my favourite bosses of all time in zombies. The fact that he has a ranged attack first and after you harm him enough, he starts to run at you is amazing. I don't think he's to difficult, nor do I think he's too easy.
And the Clowns. Oh, the Clowns... I think they are a great substitute to the standard dogs we've had for the last 9 years. And I LOVE how they can almost all spawn at once. Dog rounds were always kind of on the boring side. Clown rounds after round 25 or so are hilarious if you don't shoot them as soon as they spawn. Especially with 3-4 players.
The soundtrack in this map is my favourite out of all the maps in IW zombies. The map is set in the 80s, so the setlist consists of hits from the 80s. My personal favourites are Europe's The Final Countdown, and I Wanna  Rock by Twisted Sister. You can listen to all the songs featured in Spaceland on Spotify or Youtube.
The zombies mode in this game is my absolute favourite, and I recommend everyone to give it a good chance. If you don't like CoD Multiplayer get the game for the zombies. I mean, why not? You can get the game for like 10€.
As much as I hated Black Ops 3's multiplayer, I really like this one. Everyone's heard of other people saying that IW is just a Black Ops 3.5. Well, they aren't wrong. Although the game plays like Black Ops 3, I feel like IW did everything better. The combat rigs are a balanced version of the specialist system, high caliber + flinch isn't a problem, and the maps are better.
This is something I complain about every single time I play this game. The weapon balance in this game is questionable. What's that? You thought the Brecci was OP/annoying? The Brecci was underpowered compared to the Reaver. I mean, a semi-auto shotgun that can kill in one shot? What the ♥♥♥♥ Infinity Ward?
And don't even get me started on the ♥♥♥♥ing M.2187... "Let's add the pre-patch models from MW2!" Brilliant idea...
On the good side, every gun in this game seems to be usable. There isn't a single gun that is just absolutely useless, which is a really good thing for people like me who like variety. And I really like the way they handled the DLC weapons in this game. You can earn each weapon with a specific challenge, or you can just buy the season pass and get all the weapons immediately.
I don't really mind the variant system in this game, as you can get almost all the variants through salvage. Most of the variants are really well balanced, with a few exceptions, of course. But since everyone has the Reaver unlocked at level 1, It doesn't even matter that a variant is a little better than the base weapon...
A really good thing I like about the supply drop system is that you can use the keys you earned from zombies in multiplayer, and vice versa. I already have most of the variants I wanted so I only open crates for zombies to get more fortune cards. I love the fact that I'm able to use my keys from multiplayer for the crates in zombies.
The maps in IW are really good in my opinion. Gameplay is fast and smooth, and the maps have just the right amount of flanking routes. Campers are usually easy to kill with the Rigs like the FTL jump or the Active Camo, and the maps offer enough ways to flank the campers.
The Multiplayer in IW can be extremely frustrating at times due to the weapon balance, but it's mostly a lot of fun. The movement system is fluid and cannot be abused like in Black Ops 3 due to being more limited.
Zombies mode is fantastic and has a lot of replayability.
Multiplayer is a polished version of Black Ops 3, with a questionable weapon balance.

TL;DR: This game is a masterpiece, not only gameplaywise, but also emotionally and audiovisually. A strong recommendation to anyone who even remotely likes the exploration platformer genre often referred as "Metroidvania". An addictive game, that I personally think is one of the best eploration platformers, maybe ever. And no need to wait for a sale: BUY IT! Totally worth the money.
The long version:
The first time I read some preview about Ori and the Blind Forest, it sounded too good to be true. A really beautiful exploration platformer, that should have fair challenge and great gameplay from a brand new team, which is scattered all around the world. Yeah, I guess I can't be blamed of being a bit skeptical.
But, oh boy, oh boy, was my skepticality proven wrong. This game is exactly what was promised.
First the good things: When you see even one screen of this game, it is pretty obvious, that the game is one of the most beautiful and athmospheric platformers ever made. It is just drop dead gorgeous and it is also accompanied with emotional soundtrack, that suits the game very well.
Ori also plays great. It even manages to introduce some new elements to the formula via unlockable abilities. The abilities and game mechanics manage to keep the gameplay fresh from start to finish. And I really liked, that the game's duration is somewhere between 8-10h depending of your playstyle and platforming abilities (this one has some really challenging, BUT FAIR, sections), it kept the game "quality over quantity". I won't spoil anything about the "boss battles", but I really liked what they did here. Also the saving system is something I really liked. It's kind of a compromise from the traditional way and save anywhere.
The level design is really good. The art varies just the right amount to keep things fresh, but not confusing, and so does the challenges. There are variety of challenges, some requiring combat, some precision platforming and some require wit. At one point in the game I missed the genre standard teleport rooms, but as I went further, I realized, that he world map was connected and objectives placed so well, that it wasn't a problem anymore. And what about secrets and places you can reach later? Yep, all there.
Usually the story is just something you want to skip in platformers, but I have to say, that Ori managed to capture my attention. And the ending... Won't spoil anything. All I'm gonna say: it's beautiful.
So, what about the negative things? Like most games, this game isn't pure perfection either:
In the beginning of the game the controls feel a bit floaty, or just something little that is off. But it's no problem during the most of the game, especially as you get one ability unlocked in the relatively early part of the game, that gives you a lot more control. Also it felt, that my brains adjusted pretty quick to the floatiness. But there's few precise sections where that mattered a bit.
Some of that gorgeous art does not come without caveats. There are few places, where you don't quite realize, that something is harmful and some places where it's a bit hard to notice what is on backgroud and what on foreground. But like I said, there are only few places like this and once you realize what is what, there's no problem anymore.
All in all the problems this game have, are so small compared to the good things, that it don't matter a lot and don't hamper the overall enjoyment. As a person who enjoys Relic Entertainment's games and has an interest in the Warhammer 40,000 universe, Space Marine has been a very enjoyable experience for me.
One of the main factors that can be attributed to this is that the combat in the game is quick, brutal and satisfying. You are given a decent amount of weapons to choose, which are made up of your pistols, bolter automatic rifle, a choice of two heavy weapons and a melee weapon. Besides that, you also get to use dismountable stationary weapons and equip various Space Marine equipment and wargrear for some parts of the game. On top of that, the game encourages aggressive play due to the absence of a cover mechanic, and the only ways to regain health are either through Executions or Fury Mode, where you need to kill enemies to charge it up. Also, switching between melee and ranged combat seems pretty natural as their default buttons are on the mouse, besides the fact that enemies tend to be your face in this game. Grenades are in the game, but it's only made of a sigle type, which is the HE version. That being said, it does not detract from the overall enjoyability of the combat. And one more thing, this game has a TON of gore, which definitely helps it feel rooted in the WH40k universe.
The campaign mode of the game has a fair amount of fun and challenging missions, in addition to a decent story. In the campaign, you play as Captain Titus of the Ultramarines, sent to Forge World Graia to help the local Imperial Guard forces to fend off an Ork WAAAAGGHHHHHH long enough for reinforcements to arrive. Travelling with you are Veteran Sergeant Sidonus and the younger Leandros (will stop here due to potential spoilers). The parts where you get the Jump Pack (in my opinion) tend to be the most enjoyable sections, but that doesn't mean that the other sections are terrible. Some sections are still pretty awesome and epic, while others fall more on to the "meh" or frustrating part. Enemies range from melee cannon fodder to hulking behemoths, and you need to plan out your engagements properly as they tend to mix the enemy unit types in order to emerge victorious. That being said, your squadmates are pretty good and can hold their own in a fight without your help most of the time (from what I've seen).
Much like the campaign, the multiplayer mode of the game is also quite enjoyable. You can pick between either the Co-op Exterminatus mode, or the more traditional Versus mode. In Exterminatus, you and three other players must fight your way through around 20 waves of either Ork, Chaos or Imperial forces (depending on whether or not you have the Chaos Unleashed DLC, base game co-op is only for the Space Marines) in locations inspired by the campaign. On the other hand, Versus is your typical multiplayer, where eight Imperial Space Marines are pitted against an equal amount of Chaos Space Marines in variations of Team Deathmatch and Domination. Classes in both Exterminatus and Versus are the same, meaning that you can use your custom class type for either mode. On top of that, there are tons of customization options for both factions which can be achieved by ranking up and completeing various challenges, and allowing players to make their own custom chapters and units.
To top it off, the graphics are pretty decent, and all the models are very highly detailed. That being said, the textures can be somewhat low when viewed up-close, and the environments acan be a bit drab. However, seeing as this is a WH40k game and is set on an Imperial Forge World (where just about everything is industrialized), it shoudn't be much of a bother. Also, the sounds in the game fit in well and really help immerse you in the dark, distant future of the 41st Millenium which only knows eternal war.
In conclusion, fans of both action games and Warhammer 40k should try out this game as it is fun to play, has a decent and not-too-long story campaign, and gives players a feel of whats it like to be one of the Emperor's finest warriors.

When I was a kid, I never dreamt about nightmares from bad movies like my other kid frineds. Instead in the middle of the night, my dad would wake me up and play maortal kombat 1 with me. It got to the point where it was the only thing I thought about before I went to bed.
Now I'm substantially older and despite thinking about other things a little more, fighting games wtill hold a special place in my heart. Well...GOOD fighting games rather. Mortal Kombat 9 has popped up with the old flair it once had, but I still feel like something's missing, Blazblue is SUPER fun, but not available for PC, so of course I was just in the dust because I've never particularly liked Street Fighter.
BACKGROUND:
So then Skullgirls pops onto PC, a port I've literally waited/anticipated years for. The port is WONDERFUL. The effort everyone puts into it is phenominal. Honestly. Coming from a crowdfunding IndieGoGo campaign raising almost a million dollars and NOT being Street Fighter, it's kind of a big deal.
Hand-drawn visuals are the only thing to grace this game and it never gets old seeing each frame of animation play out...unless you're losing probably lol. While playing BlazBlue I used to occasionally play in Mike Z's lobby when he got on, but I didn't really know who he was at the time. Apparently he was like a fighting god who was a real force in gaming & I held my own against his Tager, winning and losing equally. But little did I know HE would be the guy to give input on Skullgirls and help make it, basically making it his new way to live.
SYSTEM:
Skullgirls takes out a lot of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t and just includes what's "necessary" for hardcore 2D fighters. Although there are 1 or 2 features/mechanics I wish were in the game (and might be on their way in the future), I've been pretty happy with what we have so far. everything is very straightforward and no 1-frame link ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t unless you want to make a custom combo yourself with unusual timing. And THAT'S another t hing. YOU can make combos the way you want. Implemented is something called IPS (Infinite Prevention System) that keeps people from performing infinites. Now this doesnt mean you won't get your♥♥♥♥♥whipped or long combos are out the game....quite the opposite, but it DOES mean everything is FAIR. If someone resets a combo, you'll know because of visual cues. If you keep getting hit before your attack comes out, the game will let you know with a red flash over your character, telling you you were just a biiiiit too slow and got counterhit. The system is simple, yet has depth for hardcore gamers as well.
GAMEPLAY:
To bring something new to fighting games, skullgirls combines the 6-button gameplay of something like street fighter, but mixes it with the combo-heavy nature of games like a BlazBlue. And also a really cool team-system is used. If you like playing solo with one character, you can use a REALLY strong character who has incredible damage, or trade a little bit of that for a team of 2, with regeneration when tagged out, invaluable tag assists, and Delayed Hyper combos. Things like make fighting games. It plays like BUTTER and the sense of impact is PERFECT. When you hit someone with a strong attack, you will definitely feel it. And I really like that. Wonderful sound design, everything.
CONCLUSION:
And speaking of hardcore gamers, the general pool of people who play this is one of quality. You will definitely be facing some good competition. And I'm very happy about that. So if you want to play this game, I definitely recommened it. The people are GREAT and will help you if you need it, and with nothing but more good features coming to it, it'd be best to hop on now while it's still early!

I think the overall experience I've had with the Division has been fairly good. The levelling experience is not too bad, and the story is okay, though it did feel like you were supposed to care a bit more than you actually do, which happens with games that rush storytelling and don't actually let you have a character that feels very unique (i.e. you are basically a mute clone very similar to any other player character, because of very few customization options, who obeys the orders of some random person you meet in the start of the game, for some reason).
Performance-wise the game runs pretty well on my soon outdated gtx770 and i5-4440 on high settings. The best thing about the game I'd say is probably the amazing graphics, as well as the atmosphere, which is pretty spot on for the apocalyptic genre.
I do think the game is probably the most fun when you reach the level cap, but this is also where a lot of people might stop playing immediately, as you have to the choice to A: grind PvE content you've already done (or buy the DLCs and do the incursions), B: jump into the Dark Zone to grind/PvP, which depending on the kind of person you are might be frustrating or fun, or C: do both. Personally I like doing both PvE and PvP, but I do feel like overall the game lacks a bit of content as you can easily get bored replaying story missions for daily loot for the nth time, and at some point you will have experienced all that the Dark Zone has to offer and likely be annoyed at all the kids screaming into their microphones at the top of their lungs.
Sadly Steam doesn't let you grade on a scale, but I do think this at best is an above average game, though I did enjoy the time I've spent with it enough to be able to give it a "yes" rating.

I put this game down since about 2013 and just picked it back up again - I can't wait to stop playing it again.
The thing that I hate most about this game is that it purports itself as being a "rhythm game", whereas it lacks the telltale audio cues of a rhythm game: the note that would make more sense as the audio cue note is actually the note that plays when you pass an obstacle. This game is actually a game with an admittedly nice soundtrack, but lacks the CORE component of rhythm games which allows you to lose yourself in the music. Instead, I'm here at the edge of my seat trying to anticipate when the note is going to play in order to judge when I should perform an action.
This game would be a LOT, LOT better if you could shift the audio latency such that the notes played in game could ACTUALLY serve as audio cue notes, to allow this to be an ACTUAL rhythm game.
If you're looking for a good rhythm game, instead check out Crypt of the Necrodancer, Audiosurf; people who truly love rhythm games WILL NOT enjoy this game.

Nobody gives a♥♥♥♥♥♥if you hate futuristic CoD games, especially not me. The theme alone doesn't make it bad, it's likely you are bad instead.

______
A couple points I feel like elaborating on:
Infinite Warfare's trailer was reported as one of the most disliked videos on YouTube.
Then the game eventually came out, and a whole lot of people took it upon themselves to review the game in an extremely negative way (that still happens, as far as I see). The main reason? The "futuristic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t that ruined it all". Or the fact that "CoD games beyond modern times make absolutely no sense".
But I am not one of those people, thank goodness.
Infinite Warfare is certainly a bold challenge for developers. After all, they're not creating a story that puts you in the middle of an event that has really happened (WWII), a familiar setting nonetheless (Modern Warfare) or an invented one that still retains some plausibility and similarity to it (Advanced Warfare). You are creating a future setting which forces you to use some inventive, and I'm not talking about weapons alone. Science fiction presence is strong in this game, just as it is in any other sci-fi movie or game.
The only complaint I would have about Infinite Warfare is the return of booster movements.
Boosters limit quite a bit the array of viable weapons one can bring in a match, and the habit of creating maps where marksmen will find themselves at an inevitable disadvantage only reinforces that limit. Out of 3-4 players, one is likely to whip out a spam-friendly weapon (like the Reaver or the Type-2) and just Rambo-run through the map.
One would say this system is better in that it discourages camping, but - alas - it's not that effective against them (runners constantly trip on camper traps anyways). I have been on both ends of run-and-spam tactics, so that gave me some much needed experience for my opinion.
Sure, you can also open a custom lobby and disable booster movements. Not as effective as just plugging yourself into the public matchmaking, but if you are member of a group that loves the game but dislikes boosters, this is for you. There are also "tactical gamemodes", but they are scarcely populated (if ever) so I wouldn't count on them (unfortunately).
And, as always, I would have loved an even bigger selection of weapons.
______
So, in the end...
It pains me to see such a trend for negative reviews and I have the feeling it's not because the game is inherently that much trash. Rather, people hate it because it's not Modern Warfare or WWII. Which is like saying I hate WWII because it's not cyberpunk. Maybe I should thank them, because they only made me more curious to take it up, and I'm glad I did. Also, one of my favourite cyberpunk games is about to die for good and, although Infinite Warfare is no exact equivalent and/or replacement, it does an excellent job at giving me a good futuristic experience.
It's not a thing that I see everyday: the versatility of CoD combat system (although a bit rewarding for rushers and a bit less for everyone else) and a great sci-fi setting. Infinite Warfare rewarded me with both. Add a good campaign with a captivating, desperate story and characters that you are going to love (and miss)... how could I hate it?
I wish Infinity Ward made more games like this, but I'll have to manage with this one until they decide to give sci-fi a second try.

Happy 1st anniversary my most beloved game! It has been such a long and interesting year for me with this game. Still to this day, I can't write a proper review for this game, because of how much I like it and how much love is built up inside me so that I can't even express it. I daily checked Charlie Intel for any COD 2016 news since New Year. When I first saw the reveal trailer for this game, I was like "oh pleease, another futuristic COD? Seriously? C'mon I was hoping for a modern one! But then again the leaked cover image looked nothing like one, that I saw on Charlie Intel." I saw the dislikes and got surprised, but by the time I saw the trailer the dislikes were barely 10K because how early I saw it since I was sent a notification and I instantly tapped on it, but the L/D ratio was very negative.
Eventually I grew more and more addicted and interested in the game, impatiently waiting for the release. I also fought many people in the reveal trailer's comments section and various other social media, saying that IW's hate was unjust.  Then I followed up and counted down for the E3 showcase, and I absolutely loved it! And then IW finally got the pre-order function on Steam, so I used all the money I saved up for it. Throughout the summer 2016 I was so much bored and didn't know what to do, playing bo3 made me sweat from boredom and I grew extremely tired of it (even tho I got addicted into SOE Easter Egg hunting). Then Comic Con dropped, I even got more and more hyped and excited for the game, I definitely loved the Campaign footage, and the cast was just amazing.
Then I decided to make a thread here on Infinite Warfare Steam Discussion Forums out of hype, which is entitled "This Game Is Going To Be Game Of The Year 2016!". You can find it here in the forums, it's currently the most commented on thread in this whole forums. I took my time endlessly arguing and fighting off many-many haters out there. In the end it was worth it, I successfully told them off that everyone's opnion should be respected and it was about time haters ceased bashing me for my opinion, calling me a cod kid and all sorts of stuff. It's archived now, but you still can read through if you have the time.
Time passed, the zombies and multiplayer reveal trailers released, and I couldn't get even more hyped. There was a beta arc going on, but I couldn't play it as I am on PC. The only thing left for me to do was to just wait for the release.
November 4th came, the game got released. It was so awesome, tried mutliplayer with my friends first, dope...; days later finished the campaign and I couldn't be more thrilled and exhilirated, the story was so epic and aura-giving. I also couldn't be more hestiant to shredding tears, it was so damn good, and I also liked the little easter egg at the end of the credits, gets me everytime.
Then I spent the whole year playing this awesome game, without even realizing how fast time flew by.  So yeah, that pretty much sums it all up, I'm never gonna go back to past-set games, only modern and future (and in between). I'm gonna get the game on Chirstmas tho, at least I'm planning to, mostly because of the vast player count, which IW didn't get. Now I can't play the game anymore, Infinite Warfare is now deserted.
The only thing that is left for me to do is wait, as I have started a mental campaign for the road to Infinite Warfare 2 and Infinite Warfare 3. Yes, I have high hopes for them, especially when they flirted about it and mentioned them during summer; it got my pump up so damn high.

This may be the greatest PvP game I have ever played. And to be clear, I have played literally almost every MMORPG ever made, all on PvP servers, and all were pretty inadequate. My entire gaming career has been PvP, since the days of text based online MUDs. I'm old. Whatever.
Question 1: Do you like sailing ships? If no, then don't get this game.
Question 2: Do you enjoy "war simulation" pacing? If you need constant action, then don't get this game.
Question 3: Do you like PvP? If yes, and if also yes to questions 1 & 2 then get this game.
I cannot speak as to whether PvE players will like this game. I feel the PvE content is not rich enough by itself. There is 1 PvE server (and 3 PvP servers) as of right now and I have no idea why anyone plays the PvE server.
Grind warning: there is some 'grind'. Your starter ship is limited fun and it may take you a dozen hours or more to really get out of it. That said, it is actually an effective PvP ship (no, seriously, try it in a group of like 5 of them and just go wolfpack hunting. You'll be surprised. To a big ship it's like being attacked by a swarm of killer bees) and you can participate in "Small Battles" off the Missions screen, that are basically PvP arena/cage matches. These "Small Battles" aren't a focus of the game but for a new player they can be a way to hop into quick fights for gold and XP until you're ready to try the open sea.
When you're ready for the real game, it's there, and it's a pretty epic wargame. Imagine EVE if the combat didn't suck. Imagine Planetside with a world map strategy and resource control component. Imagine Pirates of the Burning Sea without the draconian "fair fight" mechanics that broke up your groups and guilds.
This IS early access.
Expect map wipes.
Expect gold and asset wipes.
Expect some crude interfaces for areas of the game that have not been fleshed out yet.
The devs have said they will never reset our XP but anything else is on the table.
If you can accept that then just get it. It really is the best GROUP FRIENDLY PvP experience I have ever had.

TL;DR: This game is a masterpiece, not only gameplaywise, but also emotionally and audiovisually. A strong recommendation to anyone who even remotely likes the exploration platformer genre often referred as "Metroidvania". An addictive game, that I personally think is one of the best eploration platformers, maybe ever. And no need to wait for a sale: BUY IT! Totally worth the money.
The long version:
The first time I read some preview about Ori and the Blind Forest, it sounded too good to be true. A really beautiful exploration platformer, that should have fair challenge and great gameplay from a brand new team, which is scattered all around the world. Yeah, I guess I can't be blamed of being a bit skeptical.
But, oh boy, oh boy, was my skepticality proven wrong. This game is exactly what was promised.
First the good things: When you see even one screen of this game, it is pretty obvious, that the game is one of the most beautiful and athmospheric platformers ever made. It is just drop dead gorgeous and it is also accompanied with emotional soundtrack, that suits the game very well.
Ori also plays great. It even manages to introduce some new elements to the formula via unlockable abilities. The abilities and game mechanics manage to keep the gameplay fresh from start to finish. And I really liked, that the game's duration is somewhere between 8-10h depending of your playstyle and platforming abilities (this one has some really challenging, BUT FAIR, sections), it kept the game "quality over quantity". I won't spoil anything about the "boss battles", but I really liked what they did here. Also the saving system is something I really liked. It's kind of a compromise from the traditional way and save anywhere.
The level design is really good. The art varies just the right amount to keep things fresh, but not confusing, and so does the challenges. There are variety of challenges, some requiring combat, some precision platforming and some require wit. At one point in the game I missed the genre standard teleport rooms, but as I went further, I realized, that he world map was connected and objectives placed so well, that it wasn't a problem anymore. And what about secrets and places you can reach later? Yep, all there.
Usually the story is just something you want to skip in platformers, but I have to say, that Ori managed to capture my attention. And the ending... Won't spoil anything. All I'm gonna say: it's beautiful.
So, what about the negative things? Like most games, this game isn't pure perfection either:
In the beginning of the game the controls feel a bit floaty, or just something little that is off. But it's no problem during the most of the game, especially as you get one ability unlocked in the relatively early part of the game, that gives you a lot more control. Also it felt, that my brains adjusted pretty quick to the floatiness. But there's few precise sections where that mattered a bit.
Some of that gorgeous art does not come without caveats. There are few places, where you don't quite realize, that something is harmful and some places where it's a bit hard to notice what is on backgroud and what on foreground. But like I said, there are only few places like this and once you realize what is what, there's no problem anymore.
All in all the problems this game have, are so small compared to the good things, that it don't matter a lot and don't hamper the overall enjoyment. It is a true gem of craftmanship and love to the platforming genre. It pushes things forward and don't settle just copying things from old games. A HUGE recommendation! BUY IT! Don't wait sales, just BUY IT! Totally worth the money.

Well, the game's pretty short, linear and simple, you just go and do where and what you're told to do. But you can't consider this a fault, as this is all free. It looks like a demo to show the developing team's capabilities. And that's fine as I can see good potential.

Well, since it's free, you might as well play it, but listen up, this is the ONLY reason I'm not giving this a thumbs down.
If that's good enough for you, ignore the rest. However, in case you do care, I will now explain why I did not really like the game:
For one, if you think this might be a fun experience like the Stanley Parable, only because some of the same names are attached to it, you'd be dead wrong. Some even called it a sequel, which is just misleading. Sure, game-play wise, it has similarities. (Not that Stanley Parable had a lot of actual 'gameplay' going on.)
However, that's only superficial. There is no choices in this, no deeper underlying themes, no exploration and no replayability. What you get in return is a painfully unfunny 'narrator' who doesn't have one tenth of the wit that Kevan Brighting had.
The best way to describe the experience would be thus:
Imagine you are playing the Stanley Parable, but, you can ONLY do what the narrator tells you, because alternate paths aren't open, paths that you need to take don't open until you're told do go there, doors close behind you as soon as you pass to make backtracking impossible, there is no broom closet, and if you choose to ignore the narrator's command, the game simply doesn't progress until you do, and he stops reacting after a second or so. Even if you are made believe that you have only a certain time to do something, that is plainly a lie. You can take your sweet time with everything, because not doing what you're told to do is NOT an option here.
So yeah, that would be like 10 minutes that it takes to play through the Stanley Parable obeying every command, see that cheesy mind control ending, and that's ALL. That is what this game is. Everything that made the Stanley Parable good has been surgically removed. I've tried to break sequences, explore, find optional buttons and paths, anything, but there's just nothing. There's even a sequence where you are told to push certain buttons on a numeric keypad, but no matter what you do, the same thing always happens as long as you push something. Always. Second playthroughs reveal nothing new.
So don't get me wrong, I LOVE the Stanley Parable, but this is nothing like it. Maybe there's a point the developers tried to prove with this super linear and amazingly short gameplay, but I can't see it.
I almost said this is more of a demo than an actual game, but even THEN I shouldn't really recommend it because the Stanley Parable has an excellent and fun demo that is ALSO for free. So you should play that instead if you haven't yet.
If you have, play this game only if you have like 10, 15 minutes that absolutely need killing and you're not in the mood for Clash Royale or some other mobile game..
Oh, but there is a tiger in it and I love tigers.. so that's another plus in the game's favor. Don't tell me I can never say anything good about anything.

This is another example of why I wish Steam used a star rating system instead "Recommend or Not".
I'm giving The Division a "Do Not Recommend", but it's really right on the line, and is very dependent on what you are looking for.
Pros --
In honesty, I am not qualified yet to detail these as Pros.  The main reason I purchased The Division was because of the addition of a "Diablo" style end game, where you can dial in the difficulty and farm for loot, either solo or with friends or in a pick-up-group.  This really appealed to me, since I just wanted to log in, shoot some NPCs, get loot, and log out.
However, I'm still leveling.  I've already gotten burn-out without actually testing this end game.  If I'm extrapolating my leveling experience, however, I don't think it would be as fun as I anticipated.
I will say, however, that a large Pro is how much effort the Devs put into this game to enhance it, balance it, and address player feedback.
Cons --
-Not much variety in playstyle.  This may be different as you have more group play, but while leveling you basically have your sniper rile for range, and assault rifle for everything else.  I very much wanted to play a revolver using gunslinger, but sidearms are worthless, at least while leveling. (I think you can get some good gear sets later on to boost the effectiveness.  But even then, I don't know how that would compare to, say, an assault rifle build.)
-Bullet Sponge Enemies.  You will hear this a lot.  What they *don't* tell you is why this is so annoying.  It's because you are still a delicate flower.  It gets very aggravating when you can take so much damage so easily, while tougher enemies last forever.
This may just be a leveling issue.  Maybe when you are farming end-game you are invincible.  I don't know.  But I'm doing every low-level mission I can, and I still feel like I'm scraping by. (maybe my gear is too weak, but if my gear isn't keeping up naturally to my level then that's another problem.)
-A lot of time limit encounters, or run-for-cover encounters.  I'm finding a lot of the missions have enemies that spawn that you have to prevent from destroying an objective that's annoyingly far away.  Or, you walk into a space, and enemies jump you, but there isn't any ideal cover.  So you have to keep sprinting around.
Honestly, neither one is overly difficult.  i don't think I've even failed one of these missions (though I've come close since I take so much damage).  But it just *feels* annoying.  Maybe I'm playing this game with too much of a Skyrim/ESO mentality (slow, steady, tactical, instead of run'n'gun).  This is all personal preference, but to me personally this is a Con.  If the end game was exactly like this, I'd be fed up.  My only hope is that when I get to end game, it becomes a lot easier and more enjoyable for casual play.
-Complicated loot.  The community is great for answering questions.  I had some suggestions on builds to search for.  But sheesh, they are so complicated!  And I think loot is completely random, so to have a build that has all the synergies it needs, it will take a while and require a lot of bank space and management as you build it up.
Some people find this a lot of fun.  I do too to a smaller extent.  But to play this as a casual game, it's kind of off putting.  Maybe when I get to max level I'll find it's not as complicated as it sounds, but right now I really just don't have much of a drive to try and do so.
In conclusion, this is all based on preference, so take it with a grain of salt.  I wish I could rate this game a 5 out of 7 stars instead of a straight up "not recommend" to give it credit where credit is due.

I am not the best with reviews... so here goes a quick attempt to help whoever wants to know a little more info on The Division.
So I first got this game on Xbox One and I loved it. I beat the game, went through Dark Zone and probably had over 100 hours clocked in. The loot was so much fun to grind for, not as good as lets say Diablo 3, but there is still a reason to go after loot.
I then regot the game on PS4 because I had friends who also had the game. This is when I first got into the co-op scene and oh my god is this game so much better with friends.
Skip to a couple months ago and I got it again on PC for dirt cheap on some sale. I have now beat the campaign a third time and yes it was a bit stale because it can get a bit repetitive. The grind is a lot of fun from start to mid - game. But end game there doesn't feel a like a real point to grind that much.
My biggest problem with the game is the "spongenious" on the enemies hit box. The bosses have NO difference what so ever between them. They are just a big a.s.s. enemy who scares the s.h.i.t. out of you because they come out of no where and have a bigger shield and health bar. Besides that no real difference which kind of sucks.
My pros for the game are as such
-Amazing graphics, the graphics got so much better from release day no problem here
-PVE content is pretty good IMO, all missions are also replayable on different difficulties so you can approach missions differently on each mission and make each one either harder or easier on yourself.
-I also love the gear sets. Its not the best ever but the exotics and talents each set gives you is a lot of fun and adds many many more hours to gameplay to achieve which ever set/sets your going for. When this game started to die out on me, this update gave me 20 hours extra play time and counting.
- The abilites and perks and talents that this game gives you is also a lot of fun and adds a different approach you can take on many things, you can be a mix of a healer, tank, and attack with the options they give you!
- The PVP isnt the best but its also exciting and difficult. Ive heard of other people there are hackers, but I honestly havent run into any on any console.
- Cant forget about the Dark Zone. This and underground (DLC), are the most fun end game. The thrill from running in, stealing loot from other players they achieved and either continuing your journey while getting a full backpack or deciding to return because you achieved the Exotic item you needed....... but you have to wait for the extraction which gives other players enough time to hunt you down and possibly kill you!
- Survival! This game mode (DLC) is also so much fun. Adds a COMPLETELY different game mode to the stage and these "games" can last EASILY up to 2-3 hours... if you can surviva that long.
Cons
- Once you beat the main story , it does get a bit stale but with the Underground operations and Dark Zone, there is just so much more content to be played.
- One small issue that was brought to my attention was there was no search bar for your backpack. Honestly not a huge deal for me since I like to clean my stash up quickly after almost every mission but it might be nice to have because if you just run and gun for a couple hours and need to sort through your gear it would make it a bit easier to locate. They do have loadouts so itll be easier to switch to certain guns if needed.
- I did also see some performance issues like FPS drop but thats really about it. This game is not that great on a low end PC though, my PC is about mid range to high so I havent bumped into to many problems.
In the end I would 100% say this game is worth the price. If you want to wait for a sale when it jumps down to $20, which is typically does a lot, then i'd say to definitly pick it up! As you read before, I bought this game on each system and thought it was worth it each time. I created a new character each time and easily got around 50 hours on each account.
TL;DR
A lot of fun solo, even more fun co-op. Campaign is pretty good nothing amazing. If you enjoy Diablo looting grindiness and third person shooters then this game is for you!

After just having beaten this game, I need to have a long hard think about whether it's my favourite thing I've ever played in twenty years of gaming. Right now, I'm leaning towards yes.
Every now and again you get a game that just nails everything spot on. The visuals are the best I have ever seen in any video game, period. Ori is a testament to how beautiful art design will always trump polygon counts and graphical fidelity, and its visuals are likely to age better than perhaps any other video game made to date. I expect it will be a long, long time before anything else comes along that can trump the sheer beauty of Ori.
The gameplay is some of the best I have ever experienced. Tight controls, a complex variety of skills to use, and absolutely phenomenal level design that ensures it makes full use of the increasingly numerous abilities the player has right up until the end. Nothing ever felt like a gimmick, and playing this game was such a joy that I would gladly bounce around the world of Nibel for hours just to enjoy the way Ori runs, jumps, dives, glides, and swims.
And the music? It's the emotional core that holds it all together. The enchanting soundtrack will have most players crying at the beginning, crying at the end, squeeing in excitement during the dramatic sequences, and wide-eyed in wonder at the haunting scenes they traverse over the course of their adventures.
Is Ori a perfect game? Very nearly. There is, unfortunately, only one slight ding on its perfection.
By and large the game allows you to set your own difficulty in an incredibly intuitive, organic fashion, by allowing the player to create save points at almost any time (at the cost of a cooldown, and diminishing some of Ori's magical power). Despite having some incredibly challenging segments, even relatively inexperienced platformer players should be able to beat most of the game without too much difficulty, due to the frequent ability to save.
I say *most* of the game, because Ori breaks this perfect system at three critical points during the experience. There are no bosses, but rather three lengthy escape sequences that involve lots of instant death mechanics, a race against the clock, and by far the most difficult challenges contained within the game. These sequences have no checkpoints, and you cannot save during them.
As someone who's been playing platformers all my life, the only sequence that gave me much trouble was the final one, but I've heard tales of many players getting stuck and giving up as early as the first, and I empathise with them completely. The game allows anyone to complete 90% of its content -- and I'm sure many people would be drawn to this one for the art, music, and story alone -- yet forces them into bottlenecks that seem hell-bent on making less experienced players get frustrated and quit. It's fine for a game to be as challenging as Ori is during the escape segments, but it's a huge misstep to coax the average joe or jane in with such a forgiving save system, only to hit them with three increasingly difficult brick walls after a couple of hours.
However, this is the only part of the experience that mars perfection, and for more hardcore players it's not much of an issue. I hope the devs patch in optional checkpoints for these sequences, because I feel like a lot of players might currently be missing out on most of what Ori has to offer due to the difficulty roadblocks.
Overall, though? Amazing, incredible, sublime game. A true work of art if ever there was one. Due to the issue mentioned above, it falls just shy of perfection, but as someone who wasn't too punished by the escape sequences, I know I'll certainly go away from Ori with a little more light in my heart. <3

Over the countless years, I’ve probably encountered over a dozen or more “pirate” games for PC. From Cutthroats to Sea Dogs. From Sid Meier’s to Buccaneer to even getting The Patrician series as it had sailing ships in it.
However, I’ve played nothing that is quite like this. Bar, maybe, the sea battles of Sea Dogs. But this categorically leaves Sea Dogs in Davey Jones’s locker along with the rest of the afore mentioned.
I’m not saying those games are bad. That’s not true. I played Cuttroats in the 1990’s for hour upon hour. Hunting for that all but elusive Spanish treasure galleon.
I just loved the fact that you had a PC game and you could do ANYTHING you wanted to do. They are all an open book to be written as you feel fit. Though, some did have a story line that you could follow, if you so desired.
Naval Action is, in my opinion, stunning. The graphics. The ships. You can even build your own ship!! The sea battles. The game play. OK! It may not be for some. I’m sure that some will find it a little tedious to sail from place to place. But I find it tedious that a lot of PC games are just "wham, bang, thank you mam", type of games where there very little thought, but lots of action.
The fact that in Naval Action, you CAN and WILL get lost in the middle of the Caribbean Sea is... Is... Something to be really proud of.
Most likely, you’ll get lost by your own stupid human error. Setting sail from Cuba, you’re headed south to Jamaica. All is OK for the first 10 minutes. Then 10 minutes ends up being 20 minutes and it is now that you start to look around the sea for signs. ANY signs. No Land. No Ships. Not even a flippin’ Albertros to blame. It’s getting dark. The sun’s setting and there’s a mist spreading over the becalming sea. That picture had taken your mind away from your immediate predicament. But regardless, you still watch it slowly setting.
Then it’s back to reality.
Where the heck am I?
What direction did I put myself in?
So you check. Why was I heading South East, when I just needed to head South?
Oh! Well. At least the designers of the game have given you and “emergency beacon” to use. Use it and it lets you teleport back to your capital city. Depending on which of the numerous nations you decide to choose from at the beginning of the game.
But this is almost a use once option. You use it and afterwards, you cannot use it again for another 3hours of game play. So it is to be used at your discretion and used wisely.
So, in summing up.
If you like the tall ships of the 18th century (And frankly, who doesn’t?).
If you would like to command one (And who wouldn’t?)?
If you like the Caribbean?
If you like a thoughtful game, which has enough intense action in battles, then getting this game would be a most welcome and very wise move, on your part.
Sadly, I have to go now and sort my rat infested ship. Then off to try and sort out my flea infested, pox ridden scurvy crew by keeping their tempers blithe with a barrel or two of rum.
Oh! Well. The life of an 18th century ships commander isn’t all about treasure, rum, wooden legs, walking the plank and warm seas. It’s not about loosing off a broadside of cannons against some foe and, well, finding the curvaceous talents of the even looser women found in some stinking drinking hole in a place they deem fit to call a port.
“So. Arr! Vaass, mateys. I ‘ope to see ye in Port Royal one day. Now... Where’d me flippin’ parrot get to?”.

Given that I was not convinced about this game's quality, I wanted to try It, and I have to say that I understimated It because of its low price.
Is a 2D adventure game with apparently very simple dynamics, but It has a lot to offer to the players. The protagonist, a man with the only wish of reaching the moon, seemingly inexplicable, is dying; so he asks over Doctoress Eva Rosalene and Neil Watts, who belong to the sigmund Agency of Life Generation, in the attempt of reaching his very last wish through artificially implanted memories. However, as the game progresses, the plot thickens and the introspection and the past of the poor elderly protagonist, Johnny Wyles, begins to excite the minds even colder.
The graphics do not excell but they offer simple and different scenarios. The plot, at least to me, is very reminiscent of Inception (for those who saw it), even if we are talking about memories and not dreams. Johnny and his poor wife are deeply characterized, so much that the gamers are made aware about the wife's health condition, which is not so rare in today's reality. The soundtracks are very impressive, and in any case always suited to the circumstances in which they find themselves. The gameplay is very simple, but the depth of the story manages to entertain the gamer to everyone for the duration (albeit brief) of the game. Yes, the game, unfortunately, is short-lived, but nevertheless It's an experience recommended to all.
Do not be fooled by the low price, as It previously happened to me: It's a MUST HAVE in your Steam Library
Sono venuta in possesso di questo gioco grazie al consiglio di un amico, che già lo possedeva. Non convinta dell'eccellenza di tale titolo, ho voluto provarlo, e devo dire di averlo sottovalutato per via del prezzo basso.
To the moon è un'avventura grafica in 2d che si presenta come un gioco dalle dinamiche molto semplici che tuttavia ha molto da offrire ai giocatori.  Il protagonista, un uomo con il solo scopo di raggiungere la luna, apparentemente inspiegabile, è in fin di vita; così convoca nella sua abitazione sopra una scogliera i dottor Eva Rosalene e Neil Watts, appartenenti alla Sigmund Agency Of Life Generation, intento a raggiungere il suo ultimo desiderio attraverso l'impianto di ricordi artificiali. Tuttavia, man mano che il gioco avanza, la trama si infittisce e l'introspezione ed il passato del povero anziano protagonista, Johnny Wyles, inizia ad emozionare anche le menti più fredde.
La grafica, pur non eccellendo, offre scenari diversificati e semplici. La trama, almeno a me, ricorda molto Inception (per chi l'ha visto), anche se qui si parla di ricordi e non di sogni. La caratterizzazione di Jhonny e della sua povera moglie è ben approfondita, tanto da sensibilizzare la gente sulla condizione di quest'ultima, che non è così tanto rara nella realtà d'oggi. Le colonne sonore sono molto suggestive, ed in ogni caso sempre adatte al contesto nelle quali si trovano. Il gameplay è molto semplice, tuttavia la profondità della storia riesce ad intrattenere il videogiocatore allo schermo per tutta la durata (seppur breve) del gioco. Ebbene sì, il gioco, purtroppo, è poco longevo, ma tuttavia è un'esperienza consigliabile a tutti.
Non fatevi ingannare dal prezzo basso, com'è successo a me, è un MUST HAVE in libreria.

I don't know if this is a good game by COD fans standards, but it is - and I say this about the singleplayer campaign, as I don't play multiplayer - a very good sci-fi action game in general.
It's actually a bit sad that it will probably be overlooked by potential players because of the Activision and "COD" in the title, because it's basically action version of the first Mass Effect in a way. You fly in, jump out on the ground, run around the map and shoot, use special powers, jump into cockpit again, do some space dogfight, hitch a ride on a dreadnought, destroy it from the inside by hacking robots to kill their own captain, jump out in the space, see a very nice cinematic story development, use galaxy map, chose some side missions, kill some dogfight aces, crash, recover, ... And all the while with Battlestar Galactica vibe (surprise attack by a terryifing enemy, bare remnants of the fleet defending, every victory is kind of a defeat and so on).
It's a fun game with solid mechanics and an interesting story. If you're reading this in 2018/19 or later, and crave for a solid action game in space/orbit but also on the ground, feel free to check it out, don't mind that it says "COD" in the title if you're not into COD. It could have been called anything else too.

I have to recommend this game, but there are conditions as to why I do recommend it. Keep these in mind while I explain
1: I got the game with the season pass on sale for around 50 Bucks
2: I have played almost every COD since COD 2 (only haven't played Advanced War)
3: I do not love COD as a franchise, the last one I preordered was MW2
Campaign:
The Story is really damn good. The plot is very interesting and holds it's own as a scifi thriller. Voice acting and cutscenes (while there are a few too many for my taste) are incredibly well done. All the big moments in the game feel absolutely amazing to play, and there are so many of them. It feels almost cinematic but you are actively playing in game so good on you COD devs. Holds up on it's own, not long enough for 60 bucks, but it won't let you down.
Zombies: This is not like WaW zombies at all, and it's actually a pretty good thing. There is this....flavor....that this iteration of zombies has that I have not seen in anything. It's quirky, it's deep af in regards to gameplay/gun modding/easter eggs, and it just comes off as well designed and overall a unique twist on a mode that I absolutely love. The only negative I would say is that the final DLC "Beast from Beyond" map is a little plain and those stupid♥♥♥♥♥demon mutant dog things are not a good placeholder for regular zombies. Too fast and annoying.
Multiplayer:
Last and certainly least is multiplayer. For perspective, the last MP in COD that I strongly liked was BO2. There is this sort of skill gap between players in online, and you will quickly know you are on the wrong side. People fly about and slide shoot you to death and tbh slide shooting is hard af, but these people somehow consistently do it. There is an aggressive learning curve well above the Titanfall-esque style of gameplay this game has. I remember playing the campaign first and thinking, "♥♥♥♥, I hope this isn't how movement works in MP or I'm boned". Sure enough, I was right. The speed and movement is solid, but absolutely way too fast for me to even warrant ever aiming down the sights in MP. IDK maybe I'm too god damn old for COD (I'm only 25), but to get twitchy enough to play this version could possibly ruin my life medically I feel. Also the servers are dead as♥♥♥♥♥♥ so good luck not playing against the super good people as they occupy a majority of the remaining players.
Overall
2 outta 3 ain't bad
I would recommend this if you have a group of friends who love zombies and you're willing to give the campaign a shot, this may be one of the best COD's you'll ever play. Only recommendation is that you wait for a sale that includes the dlc, cause each zombies map is the bomb minus "Beast". Overall, I feel fine spending the $50 for the game+season pass.
TL;DR
+Campaign
+Zombies
-Multiplayer
Spend $50 or less for game and all dlc, you'll be happy.

"A story-driven experience about two doctors traversing backwards through a dying man's memories, in order to artificially fulfill his last wish."
♥ I have finished this game ♥
This is a beautiful and well thought out game. It's no easy feat to create a story that progresses backwards in time so that you can fully appreciate the present. The game is short, which may be a perk for some and not others. I feel the length of this game was perfect. There are many references in this game, and it's fun to find them! The sound track is beautiful and really helps influence your emotions.
This game is emotion and story driven. As for gameplay mechanics, you basically walk around (using your mouse), collecting memories so that you can progress to the next period in time. You watch this dying man's life unfold from the present until he was a young child. This is a heavy dialog game, and you have to click to go through the dialog. So walking, collecting, and dialog. Each time you progress to the next point in time, you have to solve a little puzzle. The puzzles aren't that difficult, and I found it kind of fun.
You grow to really care about the characters. You sympathise with them.
If you do not shed even one little tear at the end, you might want to have yourself tested. You may in fact not be human.

IMMERSION: The primary method of immersion in this game is combat. The act of slicing up enemies with a chainsword or shooting enemies with guns. Action is kept fast, adding to the immersion. Graphically, the game is sufficient to the task, the Orks look like Orks, and the kill moves are satisfyingly bloody without crossing the line into realistic violence. The game has a plot and a story which is able to link combat arenas together suficiently. Audio design is sufficient to the purpose of reinforcing combat satisfaction, guns provide satisfying thumps, chainsaws sound like chainsaws. (8/15).
DIFFICULTY: The game has difficulty settings, but are gross adjustment only, with basic descriptions but not poor. Control schemes do not provide additional difficulty, as buttons are well mapped for easy location once tutorialised. (8/15)
LASTING APPEAL: While the game does not exactly compel the player to complete the game's story, it is engaging in short bursts. The game includes multiplayer elements, notably a horde mode called: Exterminatus. This can be played in private mode, allowing it to be played as a single player game if the player desires. This fact increases the lifespan of the game substantially, though it is again  most enjoyable in short sessions. (6/15)
Final analysis: Warhammer 40,000 Space Marine is a game designed around the central concept of satisfying combat, and it succeeds at this. Unfortunately, it succeeds at little else so well, but the combat is engaging enough. (7/15)
