Interesting game with great art and some neat combat, Chaos Reborn ultimately suffers from a lack of variety, a well-written but bland story, and a combat design that focuses too heavily on RNG.  Its multiplayer may be entertaining, however, the population of the game is already too few to easily or regualrly find matches.
After a short time of playing you burn through the content of both factions and see the futility of trying to implement so many robes, staves, and runes when only two factions are available to add variety... leaving you asking yourself why you continue to play.  While the story has some interesting events and story elements, the gameplay does not change throughout and little persistence exists.
The combat, the obvious mainstay of the game, suffers from the large crutch of RNG (a true spiritual successor to XCOM), leaving a frequent salty taste in your mouth.  The overall array of options and effects from your cards is decent and fun, but you swiftly go through all the game has to offer with nothing more in sight.
Single-player features hot-joining of random players to play as your ally or enemy, however, you will find yourself waiting as the population has significantly shrunk after release.
Overall, I would not rate Chaos Reborn poorly - it does what it has well, but ultimately lacks enough content to keep you going.  Personally, I would not pay 20$ for the current content.  However, if you're itching for a tactically-interesting, turn-based single-player game I would recommend it for less.
Edit: I have not played the game since RNG has been removed.  The entire design is focused around that, so I hope it has not taken all the life out of the game with it.

This game has problems. Yes. The controls are a bit odd to get used to and momentum still seems a bit slow to build but they're okay when you get used to them. That's not the real problem I have here. The real problem is the level design.
Crimes:
#1: ARBITRARY WAITING. No, I do not find it fun to wait around for obstacles to align in just a way to make progress possible. No, I do not find it fun to wait for literally no reason other than having a block disappear/a balloon or bubble respawn, or for a laser to deactivate. That is NOT FUN. It utterly destroys the pacing of at least half the levels. I'll go on record saying that cycle-based level design isn't particularly fun to begin with but they really go the extra mile here.
#2: Poor checkpointing. For one, this is a precision platformer where everything is instant death. You'd think more than one checkpoint in levels of this length would be mandatory. Even on top of that, some of the checkpoints are horribly misplaced. There are a few levels with the checkpoints literally right at the start and a full length level after them. There are plenty of levels with the checkpoint too early or too late so the second half is either much longer or shorter than the first half.
#3: Heavy emphasis on trial-and-error gameplay. A little bit would be fine (especially if the checkpoint system was better) but there are a decent number of levels where something will kill you that you couldn't have possibly seen coming (off the left side of the screen or from up above on vertical levels) that is just plain not fair, especially considering you could have to replay half of a level because of that. There's also lots of sections where you either have to study obstacle patterns really well or just keep trying things until you find what's intended of you. I'm not psychic, I will never be psychic, punishing me for not being psychic is pretty dang mean. This is a common problem in games, where the developer, having designed the levels, knows what's coming and doesn't see the flaws of their level.
#4: Awful, awful bosses. All 5 of them. They're very RNG heavy and two of the bosses you can't hit unless the RNG lines up for you. The third boss especially is pretty much pure luck to beat, as you have to wait for him to come down to the ground (which has taken upwards of 20 seconds for me before...) and then you have to hope you bounce high enough off him because you can't chain hits for some arbitrary reason. The battle can take a long time and you can be completely screwed over for no good reason. None of the bosses are very good though, nor fun.
There's other minor problems I have with the game (lots of tiny platforms you have to jump between, a good number of predict-the-laser-cycle parts, some awkward jumps, etc.) but those are the real dealbreakers for me. Aside from that. The collectibles are okay, though a lot of them rely on witholding information from the player (fake walls, invisible blocks, collectibles outright hidden behind scenery). The minigames... exist. I guess. I barely played around in them, they're all RNG hatefests. There's also time trials which I wouldn't dare attempt because playing through some of these levels with checkpoints and no time constraints was already frustrating enough. The graphics are meh, the music is meh, the story is nonexistent.
There's practically no difficulty curve too. I don't feel like the game ever got harder as a whole. There were always some levels that weren't too much of a challenge and some levels that were way too much of a challenge, and these are all over the place in the game. Even ignoring the (kind of clever) level progression system where you have to clear future worlds to unlock every level in a world. The ones locked weren't noticeably harder than the levels you played before in the world, or the levels in future worlds you had to play to unlock them.
Really, overall, why does this game exist, anyways? What does it bring to the table? It's a 3-button game. It is less complex than the original super mario bros controlwise. There is no wall jump. There are no powerups. You move left, right, and jump, that's it. The levels provide most of the gimmicks but there's nothing new. Bomb blocks that explode after you touch them. Bubbles/balloons you can bounce on to go higher. Lasers that turn on and off. Turrets that shoot at you. Occasional autoscroll or advancing wall segments. Nothing original or inspired. There's not really too much clever things done with these obstacles either, very little I haven't already seen before and seen done better. This feels like a product more than a labor of love. A game to fill space and to get money without anything that makes it worth the time spent playing it or the money spent buying it. Even if the level design was better, this is the real reason why I can't recommend this game. It has no reason to exist. It's the poor man's Super Meat Boy. Heck, no, it's the poor man's Mr. Bree - a game that itself is a poor man's Super Meat Boy. That game didn't have much special to it either but it at least felt like a project someone poured passion into (and it had decent levels too which helped, I guess.) And let me state for the record that I don't even like Super Meat Boy, but this game does everything Super Meat Boy does wrong way worse, and doesn't even have the feel of an ambitious indie project to make up for it.

I'm gonna start this review out by saying right away. Go buy this game immediately!
I wan't to state right away, that this is probably the best game I have ever had at my disposal. Everything from the music, to the gameplay, to the story. Is all done to the point of perfection.
The music in this game is a very big contender, to be the very best game soundtrack I have ever heard! The soundtrack is this very beautiful atmospheric music, that mostly relies on piano music with some interesting sound effects to top it. They made good use of the different soundtracks absolutely perfect! All the soundtracks in the game, is played at the very perfect time and place in the game, which ultimately helps you get a very immersive experience. That is not to say that it is only calm nice music, cause that is certainly not the case! The moment that really shines is when you have restored the water element. That leads to a sequence where you have to make your way to the top of a cave like thing, while crystal blue water is rising and splashing all around you. Now you would probably think there is some sort of action music here to raise intensity, but that is not the case in Ori. Instead of neither a calm piano soundtrack or an intense action like soundtrack. We get this outstanding adventure emtional like music, that fits so well with the circumstances. It's so that you could almost shred a tear :,)
If you were to play this game, which you totally should. Do yourself a favor and get a nice pair of headsets, cause the sounds of this world will blow you away! Every little sound you here in the forest is so perfect! I mean it all sounds so organic and convincing. If we were to give sound effects forms and figures. Ori's sound effects are really nice and firm, rather than sound effects from games like... Yeay from nearly every goddamn game out there! Take my word for it, you are gonna love it!
The gameplay in Ori is among some of the most fun I've ever had in a platformer. The gameplay is fluid and dynamic and constantly evolves the further you get into the game. Along the path on your adventure you'll come across several spirit like trees, which rewards you with different powers that'll help you surpass areas that was previously impossible to progress through. Now I don't wanna spoil what kind of powers you get, cause they are actually pretty damn cool, so I think you should find out yourself. But do know this... They are fun as hell!
If we have to take a look at the aspect of the world of Ori itself (Gameplay wise) It's a game that rewards you for exploration and finding hidden paths and sercrets. There is alot to go around when it comes to the world Ori, but one thing I should probably state is. This game is not easy! Trust me! I died 400 times before I finished the game. But the good thing about Ori is, that you never really get angry or annoyed from dying. Neither feeling it's unfair and simply way too hard. When you do die, you know what you did wrong for the most part and you never see it as an impossible task that you'll be stuck at for an hour. It's hard but fair. One last thing to mention is the save/checkpoint system. Now this is an interesting one. In Ori you have some mana like energy that can be restored by defeating some enemies aswell as destroying blue crystals. This mana energy thing is used to commence some powers, where one of those powers are checkpoints. You can place these anywhere, with some few exceptions. When you die, you spawn at your last placed checkpoint no matter how far back it were! So remember to place these frequently.
Ori and the blind forest is by far the most beautiful game I've ever gazed my eyes upon! The art style of this game is beyond fantastic. The color saturation is so prefect in every area of the game and it is by far the most immersive game world I've ever been in. You constantly have the urge to progress, just to see what gorgeous new area that awaits you! This is also one of the things that makes exploration in Ori so fun. There isn't really much else to say about the visuals of Ori, other than it's done to perfection!
Now the story of Ori is good, but isn't really FANTASTIC. It's been heard before, looking from the bigger perspective. I won't go into details here, since I think it's should be experienced first hand. But I can tell you this much, 10 min. after the game had started I nearly cried. Holy ♥♥♥♥, is the love in this game strong! The intro sequence of Ori is the most heartbreaking moment I've ever experienced in a video game. Like I said before, the story isn't really too original, but somehow they manage to make it feel original and fresh! It's definitely an interesting story to check out.
Now as you have probably figured out so far. I ♥♥♥♥ing love this game! I love it so much that it has become my all time favorite video game! This game hit me somewhere in my gamer hearth, I never thought a game could. In all honesty, I can't come up with any cons of Ori and the blind forest. This game is the very first game I've tried, that deserves the title "Perfect" And I don't care if you are not in to the platform genre, do yourself a favor and try out the game anyway. You won't regret it!

The game opens with the Larian studios logo, an image of a  stern looking warrior who is playfully popped in the head with a sucker arrow (is that what they are called?). This is a perfect analogy for divine divinity original sin. At base, its a really strong RPG with great combat mechanics and multi-layered story line involving the very destruction of time and space.
Despite this, the game manages a blanket of humour that's just enough to stop the game taking itself too seriously and subtle enough not to undermine the core game. Visuals, voice acting and game stability are all first rate and the developers continue to give up dates well after the games initial release date. Original sin is a obvious labour of love and all that time and attention shows. My personal complaints about the game are small and could even be seen as nitpicking but i wanted to share all my thoughts. Crafting feels unsatisfying and unnecessary, i wanted to explore this aspect of the game but was continually turned off after a minute or so of trying to involved. Loot, there is way too much loot. After every fight and even chest discovery i found myself constantly comparing my new find to the gear i have on. It seems every 5 mins of gameplay brings the potential of an upgrade. I didn't like this for two reasons, it breaks the immersion of the world and compelling story line i am engaged in and two, legendary items don't feel legendary, the feel common place. Lore master is also a little immersion breaking. Everything you get an item you need to find it in your backpack, right click to identify item then begin the comparison to your current gear i previously mentioned, it would be much more efficient if it just proc'ed naturally.
Despite these minor flaws  divinity is one of the greatest story driven RPG's of all time. Even the companions have compelling stories that reveal themselves over time and time in well with the main plot. The isometric RPG could be seen as played out but Larian have breathed enough fresh ideas into it that it feels like an advanced step in the games style rather than a mere throwback. The duel main character aspect was particularly refreshing. If you are sitting on the fence then i urge you to give this game a try. There is plenty bang for your buck and virtually none of it feels like filler. 9/10

It all started with a simple discussion between high school friends about upcoming games and what we were excited for—that was nine years ago. Someone had mentioned the upcoming expansion for CANCER SIMULATOR,, I promptly looked up information on the HOW TO GET RID OF IT, and after about an hour I thought to myself “This could be interesting.” Nine years later I am still playing BAD RATS, and I’m as excited as ever for the latest installment, which goes by the name of 9/11 SIMULATOR 2K17.
This will be the sixth expansion to THE NHS' immense MMO game world, which originally launched back in 2004. There have been some rocky roads travelled with past expansions—issues such as content drought and player boredom along with poorly thought out concepts in general (i.e. The Twitter integration patch)—but THE NHS will admit to their mistakes and, in the end, will usually deliver with future content. BAD RATS feels like an expansion that will improve on everything good they can deliver while attempting to keep players invested in the game. Brand new zones packed full of substance, an interesting new class, and some of the most engaging character content I’ve ever seen in the game will hopefully shape BAD RATS into an absolute monster of an GAME.
Let’s start off by taking a look at the new area we will be leveling our characters in for this expansion: The Broken Isles. The isles are made up of six zones, four of which are leveling zones. THE NHS has introduced a new concept to BAD RATS with 9/11 SIMULATOR 2K17 by having the leveling zones scale with your level. This means you can pick any of the four zones in which to begin the next stage of your adventure, something I have personally enjoyed. The new zones all look incredible in terms of landscape and art design, and each one is vastly different than the others. For example you have THE CHEMO WARD, a land full of Vikings and dragons and the mythology and lore surrounding them, but then you have a zone like THE RECOVERY ROOM, which sits at the other end of the spectrum. This zone was once the pinnacle of RATSand is where the brothers BIGGIE CHEESE AND RODDY were born. As such, it has a very elven look to it, but the land is also suffering from the corruption of WHITE IN THE GHETTO, which gives everything a beautiful but nightmarish look and this is also probably the best looking zone I’ve ever seen in BAD RATS.

Updated review as of Version 1.7:
Well after playing this game for well over a year, and with over 700 hours of playtime I think I can safely say that Chaos Reborn doesn’t have too much rng.
This is an excellent game, Classic Mode in particular feels like I'm playing the original Chaos again.
It's turn based tactics with an element of risk management – It’s easy to pick up and play your first match, and then you start to find ways to try and master it. If you like Chess and/or Poker then you'll love this game.
+Very friendly user community
+Devs who listen to their player base and who continually look to improve the gameplay experience
+A well balanced game
+Polished sound and graphics (I say this, and then they keep improving them again)
+The risk management within the game leads to variety in matches meaning that the game never gets old. I’ve played a lot of turn based stategy games which get old and repetitive, where once you learn how to play the system you’ll never have anything new to learn, Chaos Reborn isn’t like that, you’re always learning something new.
+The addition of the Custom Match Maker is wonderful. Want to play 2v2v2 in a Law vs Neutral vs Chaos battle with you mates? You can do it. Want to play 3v3 with the AI helping out on both sides? You can do it. Want to play 1v5? You can do it (you’re also going to die). ;-)
+Gooey Blob!
- 6 player mode is great, 8 player mode would be even better.
In short; a finely tuned turn based strategy game made in the vein of Chaos Battle of Wizards, by the man who defined the genre in the first place. If you want to win every match until you’re snoring over your keyboard go one of the other generic turn based games out there, if you want something infinitely re-playable come and join the fun that we’re having with Chaos Reborn.
Updated Review as of Version 1.8.
The devs have just added a new Law Mode for those who don't enjoy RNG.
Personally Law Mode is not my cup of tea (you'll find me playing Classic Chaos Mode), but you can enjoy any one of the four available game modes without having to participate in any of the others (and you could well like more than one). To that end I'd suggest trying each game mode out and before deciding whether the game as a whole is something that's for you.
What is 100% is that the devs of this game are responding to their playerbase and making regular game updates. That in itself is to be commended.

Hard to learn, hard to master, but another brilliant (re)design by J. Gollop. Turn-based tactics games with a fantasy theme are common, but the strong bluffing elements and risk management you will find here make for a unique experience. I wouldn't recommend it for impatient people, because the chance elements (random results for spellcasting) can be frustrating to those not willing to put in the time to learn how to adapt to it. This constant uncertainty is the main feature of the game.
Currently the game offers a lot of flexibility: You can play in ranked or friendly matches with strangers over the internet, play hotseat in your home, organize a team match with friends or play co-op against the computer. Either live or asynchronous play is supported, so you can play your turns when you get back from work, or play with people in different time zones.
The only negative thing I could say about Chaos Reborn, is that it has a form of DRM. But being one of the best turn based multiplayer games you will find, it's completely worth it.

Chaos Reborn is a perfect blend, taking the fine art of risk management/mitigation from timeless games like poker and adding a turn based strategy fantasy theme. The game is so good I have left my wife and job and I have not eaten in 9 months, I see this as a positive.
Chaos allows you to build your own sets of equipment, shaping the likelihood of what spells you receive and creating unique playstyles and almost infinite possible load-outs. There are realms to explore and co-op play with friends with social ranks and guilds to come
The real strength of Chaos however, comes from the PVP aspect , I have read reviews and comments about the RNG system making Chaos overly reliant on luck, this is nonsense.
% chances of spell casts and combat resolutions are displayed on screen and choosing the timing and method of attack, which spells to boost the % of or discard, when to bluff with an illusion and which tactics to use to give yourself a +expected value for victory are skills which are all required to make a good Chaos player.

I am the Community Manager for this game.
Looking at my hours on record and given my Community Manager status you will not be surprised to learn that I heartily recommend this game.
It's a fast paced tactical game with RPG elements and a consistently praised open and friendly community.  Check the forums at
for the latest discussions.
Be aware however that it does heavily use Random Number Generation so you will not win every game you play.  The core skillset here is risk management by means of manipulating your chances of success.  This is achieved by ustilising the LawChaos balance in game to enhance the chances of successful casting of Law/Chaos spells, boosting spell success chance with mana and using the illusion/bluff mechanic.
With the recent 1.7 "co-op" update it is now easy to set up games with your friends or the community at large.  In the Realms of Chaos you can even play co-op against the AI.
As I mentioned - no one wins every game but experienced players do win more often than mere RNG would suggest.
With the free demo and Steam's refund policy I would advise anyone reading this to check it out.  Look me up in game and perhaps I'll see you there!
